stances.claim: The ICC lost jurisdiction over the Philippine drug-war 'situation' (Nov. 1, 2011 - March 16, 2019) because former chief prosecutor Bensouda failed to petition the PTC for, and be granted, formal investigatory authority within one year of the effective PH withdrawal on March 17, 2019.
stances.rhetorical_move: statutory-construction conclusion (Article 127 exception requires being 'already under consideration' by the Court, not just by the Office of the Prosecutor)

stances.claim: The Office of the Chief Prosecutor is NOT an integral part of the ICC for purposes of the Article 127 'already under consideration by the Court' exception -- to render true justice, prosecutors should be separate and distinct from independent judges.

International and arbitral tribunals like the ICC use verba legis strictly because the Rome Statute did not authorize ICC judges to interpret liberally or actively -- they have no equivalent to the PH SC's grave-abuse-of-discretion duty.
stances.rhetorical_move: comparative-tribunal framing (international tribunals are bound to literalism; PH judiciary is not)

stances.claim: The PH SC is 'emphatically mandated by our Constitution with the duty -- not just the power -- to strike down grave abuse of discretion thereby commanding it to be activist, NOT literalist' -- and Civil Code Articles 9 and 10 reinforce this with the duty to decide and the presumption of right-and-justice intent.
stances.rhetorical_move: constitutional-mandate framing for PH judicial activism, contrasted with international tribunals' confinement
stances.confidence: asserted with constitutional and statutory citation

stances.claim: Equitable solutions cannot rescue the ICC here -- international jurists do NOT have the PH judiciary's ex aequo et bono privilege; per retired Justice Azcuna, only courts that are 'both courts of law and equity' may grant equitable remedies.
stances.rhetorical_move: equity-jurisdiction unavailability argument with Azcuna citation

stances.claim: Drug-war victims must not be stranded -- local investigative and prosecutorial agencies (various police, DOJ, Ombudsman, Solicitor General) must probe complaints fairly and speedily, with courts then deciding fairly and speedily once probable cause is found.
stances.rhetorical_move: victim-protection imperative (loss of ICC jurisdiction shifts duty to PH agencies)
stances.confidence: asserted as moral and legal duty

stances.claim: Without fair-and-speedy justice domestically, the drug war 'will forever be a black hole' in both Marcos Jr.'s and Duterte's legacies -- sucked into 'a maelstrom of suspicions, innuendoes, and diminutions, if not of unpardonable abuse, criminal neglect, and worse, of outright rebellion.'
stances.rhetorical_move: legacy-stakes framing (binding both administrations to the duty)

notable_anecdotes: Self-referential framing: CJ explicitly extends 'last Monday's column' (A100) to provide the legal justifications others requested, especially for 'fellow lawyers' who 'reluctantly agreed' with the loss-of-jurisdiction view.

Direct quotation of Rome Statute Article 127's exception ('shall not prejudice in any way the continued consideration of any matter which was already under consideration by the Court prior to the date on which the withdrawal became effective') as the core text he interprets.

Adolfo S. Azcuna's quote: PH justices have the privilege 'to decide ex aequo et bono -- according to one's sense of what is right and just' because PH courts are 'both courts of law and equity' -- used as the named-justice warrant for the equity-unavailability argument.
Civil Code Article 9 + Article 10 paired together as twin constraints on PH judicial conduct (cannot decline; must presume right-and-justice intent) -- both absent from the Rome Statute.
Naming of four PH agencies in roll-call sequence (various police forces, DOJ, Ombudsman, Office of the Solicitor General) to fix institutional responsibility once ICC loses its remit.
Closing prayer: 'My fervent prayer is for our Father in heaven to deliver us from this maelstrom. Amen.' -- a religious-imprecation closer that elevates the column's stakes beyond legal analysis.

one_paragraph_summary: Following up his prior Monday's column (A100) that ICC has lost jurisdiction over the Philippine drug-war 'situation' due to former chief prosecutor Bensouda's egregious failure to obtain PTC investigatory authority within one year of the PH's effective withdrawal on March 17, 2019, Panganiban delivers the legal justifications his fellow lawyers -- who 'reluctantly agreed' -- had requested. Under Rome Statute Article 127, a State Party's withdrawal takes effect one year after notice to the UN Secretary General, with an exception preserving matters 'already under consideration by the Court' before that effective date -- but the question turns on whether the Office of the Chief Prosecutor is 'an integral part of the ICC,' to which CJ answers no: 'to render true justice, prosecutors should be separate and distinct from independent judges.' Equitable solutions cannot rescue the situation either, because international and arbitral tribunals like the ICC use verba legis strictly -- the Rome Statute does not grant ICC judges the kind of activist mandate the PH Constitution emphatically gives our Supreme Court via the grave-abuse-of-discretion clause, nor the Civil Code's Article 9 (judges cannot decline to decide) and Article 10 (doubt construed in favor of right and justice) -- and per retired Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna, only PH courts as 'both courts of law and equity' may grant ex aequo et bono remedies. Still, drug-war victims must not be stranded: the various police forces, the DOJ, the Office of the Ombudsman, and the Office of the Solicitor General must probe complaints fairly and speedily, and once probable causes are determined, courts must decide fairly and speedily -- for without this, the drug war 'will forever be a black hole' in both Marcos Jr.'s and Duterte's legacies, sucked into 'a maelstrom of suspicions, innuendoes, and diminutions, if not of unpardonable abuse, criminal neglect, and worse, of outright rebellion. My fervent prayer is for our Father in heaven to deliver us from this maelstrom. Amen.'
